test_title: SSC Selection Post Graduation Level Official Paper (Held On: 28 June, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper is incurring a loss of cost price of 4 pens while selling 20 pens to Ajay. If the shopkeeper had purchased 20 pens at 10% less price and had sold 20 pens to Ajay at 25% more than the selling price, then how much percentage would he have gained (rounded off to 1 decimal place)?
solution:
**Given:-**

A shopkeeper is incurring a loss of cost price of 4 pens while selling 20 pens to Ajay 

The shopkeeper had purchased 20 pens at 10% less price and

had sold 20 pens to Ajay at 25% more than the selling price

**Formula used:- ** 

Loss = C.P. – S.P. (C.P.> S.P.) 

Profit = S.P. – C.P. 

Profit Percent = (Profit × 100)/ C.P.

Where

C.P. is the actual price of the product

S.P. is the sale price 

**Calculation:-**

Let the cost price of each pen = 1 Rs.

The cost price of 20 pen= 20 Rs

Loss = 4 Rs.

So, SP = 20 - 4 = 16 Rs

2nd part of the question, 

The shopkeeper had purchased 20 pens at 10% less price 

⇒ New CP =( 20 × 90)/100 = 18 Rs 

Sold 20 pens to Ajay at 25% more than the selling price

⇒ New SP = 16 × 125/100 = 20 Rs

Profit% = [(20-18) × 100]/18 = 200/18 = 11.11.....%

** ∴ The required answer is 11.1%**
